research_question: In children in low- and middle-income countries, what is the effect of mobile phone reminders (SMS text messages and/or phone calls, including automated voice calls) sent to parents/caregivers, compared with routine immunisation care without reminders, on receipt of the third dose of DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3 / pentavalent-3)?
treatment_label: Mobile phone reminders to parents/caregivers (SMS text messages and/or phone calls, including automated voice calls) plus routine immunisation care
control_label: Routine immunisation care without reminders (no-reminder control)
outcome_description: Number of children who received/completed the third dose of DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3 / DPT3 / pentavalent-3 / Penta-3) out of the number randomised/enrolled in each arm, at the study's main follow-up assessment for that dose (e.g. by 14 weeks, 18 weeks, 6 months or 12 months of age). Extract crude (unadjusted) event counts per arm using intention-to-treat denominators (all randomised/enrolled participants); if only percentages are reported, convert to counts using the number randomised in that arm. Do not use adjusted odds ratios, logistic-regression or cluster-adjusted (GEE) estimates when raw counts are available, and do not convert an odds ratio into the result. Where a trial reports the three pentavalent doses separately, use only the third dose (or 'completed all 3 doses'). Prefer overall receipt of DTP3 over 'timely receipt within 1 week of due date' or 'received without delay'. In multi-arm trials, use the reminder-only arm (SMS/phone call alone) versus the no-reminder routine-care arm, ignoring arms combining reminders with monetary or other incentives, education-only arms, and other co-interventions.
positive_direction: A positive effect (RR greater than 1, equivalently a positive Hedges g on the underlying scale) means MORE children received the third dose of DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3/Penta-3) in the mobile phone reminder arm than in the routine-care no-reminder arm — i.e. reminders improved DTP3 coverage.

mobile phone text message reminder vaccination coverage pentavalent third dose trial
automated voice call reminder caregivers DTP3 immunization uptake effect
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial (individual or cluster randomised) conducted in a low- or middle-income country setting

Intervention includes mobile phone reminders (SMS text messages, phone calls, or automated voice calls) sent to parents or caregivers about childhood immunisation, compared with routine care without reminders
Reports quantitative data on receipt of the third dose of DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3/DPT3/pentavalent-3/Penta-3), as event counts or percentages with arm denominators
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, protocol, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)

No comparison between a reminder intervention arm and a no-reminder control/routine-care arm, or non-randomised design (quasi-experimental, observational, controlled before-after, interrupted time series)
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no event counts, percentages with denominators, proportions, or odds/risk ratios)

Completely unrelated to the research topic (e.g. no mobile phone reminder intervention, no childhood immunisation outcome, or only non-DTP3 outcomes such as measles, BCG, OPV, yellow fever, 'fully immunised', timeliness/delay, or cost outcomes)
moderators_to_extract: Reminder modality (SMS only, phone/voice call only, or combined)
Country / World Bank income group (low-income vs lower-middle vs upper-middle)
Setting (urban, rural, mixed) and recruitment site (facility vs community)
Sample size category and baseline DTP3 coverage in the control arm
effect_size_note: Pool as a risk ratio (RR) with a random-effects model (DerSimonian-Laird or REML, with Hartung-Knapp adjustment considered given the likely small number of trials). Use crude event counts per arm with intention-to-treat denominators; convert reported percentages to counts using the randomised arm totals. For cluster-randomised trials, prefer crude counts as reported; note design effects/ICCs qualitatively in sensitivity analysis rather than substituting cluster-adjusted GEE estimates. Assess heterogeneity with I-squared and tau-squared, and publication bias with a funnel plot/Egger test if 10 or more trials are available.
single_outcome_target: receipt of third dose of DTP-containing vaccine (DTP3/Penta-3)
